title: Pan-Seared Ribeye
description: One ribeye seared hard in a smoking skillet, then basted in butter, garlic and herbs.
beforeYouStart: Have an instant-read thermometer ready: you pull the steak at 130F (54C) inside.

steps.do: Take the steak out of the fridge 30 minutes before cooking so it cooks evenly instead of staying raw in the center.
Heat the oil in the skillet over medium-high heat until it just starts to smoke, about 3 minutes. A pan that isn't hot enough won't give you a golden crust.
While it heats, pat the steak dry and season the top side. Salted any earlier, it draws out moisture and won't sear.
Lay it in seasoned side down, season the new top side, and cook without moving it: 3 to 4 minutes for a 1 in (2.5 cm) steak, 5 minutes for 1 1/2 in (4 cm).
Peel the garlic cloves, if using, and leave them whole. Strip the herb sprigs from any tough stems, and set out the butter.
Turn it, add the butter, herbs and garlic, and keep spooning the melted butter over the steak as it finishes. Pull it at 130F (54C) inside for medium-rare; it climbs about 5F more as it rests.
Rest 5 to 10 minutes before slicing and serving.

notes: Searing fat: beef tallow, bacon grease, or a high-smoke-point oil such as light olive oil or avocado oil. Not extra virgin olive oil.
Cast iron gives the deepest crust, but any heavy-bottomed pan works.
Leftovers keep 3 to 4 days in the fridge, airtight or wrapped in foil.
nutrition: Per serving (estimate): 1071 kcal · 3 g carbs · 69 g protein · 88 g fat (31 g sat) · 268 mg sodium
